name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse
shortDescription:
Expert Treatment Including Anterior Repair & Robotic Sacrocolpopexy
Pelvic organ prolapse (POP) occurs when pelvic floor support weakens, allowing the bladder, uterus, vagina, or rectum to descend. These changes can cause pressure, urinary problems, difficulty with bowel movements, or a visible bulge. POP is common and highly treatable — and RoMIUS Urology provides advanced, compassionate care for all forms of prolapse.
We specialize in minimally invasive pelvic floor reconstruction, offering a full spectrum of treatments from pelvic floor therapy to advanced robotic surgery.
body:
Types of Pelvic Organ Prolapse We Treat

Anterior Prolapse (Cystocele)

The bladder drops into the vaginal canal, often causing:

  • Pressure or heaviness
  • Urinary leakage or urgency
  • Difficulty emptying the bladder
  • Recurrent UTIs
  • A bulge at the vaginal opening

Apical Prolapse (Uterine or Vaginal Vault)

The uterus or top of the vagina descends due to loss of pelvic support.

Posterior Prolapse (Rectocele)

The rectum bulges forward into the vagina, causing:

  • Incomplete bowel emptying
  • Constipation
  • Vaginal pressure

Urethral Hypermobility

Loss of support under the urethra can cause stress urinary incontinence.

Symptoms of Pelvic Organ Prolapse

  • Pelvic pressure or heaviness
  • Sensation of a vaginal bulge
  • Urinary urgency, leakage, or retention
  • Difficulty emptying the bladder
  • Constipation or straining
  • Pain during intimacy
  • Recurrent UTIs
  • Tampon “falling out” sensation

Evaluation

RoMIUS Urology performs a comprehensive, gentle assessment that includes:

  • Pelvic exam
  • Grading of prolapse severity
  • Pelvic floor strength testing
  • Bladder emptying evaluation
  • Imaging when needed
  • Hormonal evaluation (post-menopausal changes)
  • Review of childbirth history & prior surgeries

This helps us build a personalized treatment plan tailored to anatomy, symptoms, and goals.

Treatment Options

1. Conservative Treatments

For mild to moderate prolapse or women preferring non-surgical care:

  • Pelvic floor physical therapy
  • Vaginal estrogen
  • Activity and lifestyle adjustments
  • Pessary fitting and management
  • Treatment of coexisting bladder symptoms

2. Surgical Treatment Options

RoMIUS Urology offers advanced, durable surgical solutions including:

Anterior Repair (Cystocele Repair)

Rebuilds support under the bladder to eliminate pressure, bulging, and urinary symptoms.
Performed:

  • Minimally invasively
  • With strong, natural tissue support
  • As outpatient surgery in most cases

Robotic Sacrocolpopexy (Gold Standard for Apical Prolapse)

This is the most durable, anatomic repair for apical prolapse. Using tiny incisions and robotic precision, the vagina (or uterus with hysteropexy) is restored to normal position using a supportive graft.

Benefits of Sacrocolpopexy

  • Long-term anatomic success
  • Excellent support for anterior & apical defects
  • Faster recovery
  • Minimal pain
  • High durability compared to vaginal repairs

Rectocele Repair

Restores posterior vaginal support and improves bowel function.

Urethral Support Procedures

For leakage caused by urethral hypermobility, we offer:

  • Mid-urethral sling
  • Urethral bulking
  • Pelvic floor therapy

Why Women Choose RoMIUS Urology for Pelvic Organ Prolapse

  • Expertise in anterior repairs and pelvic reconstruction
  • Advanced robotic sacrocolpopexy capabilities
  • Conservative + surgical options tailored to each woman
  • Strong integration with pelvic floor therapy
  • Evidence-based, minimally invasive approach
  • Focus on restoring confidence, comfort, and function
  • Comprehensive follow-up and long-term support
